en.question: A research assistant must handle both "what is our refund window?" and "compare our refund policy against twelve competitors and produce a report". Which design handles both efficiently?

options.text: Route both through the agent path so behaviour stays uniform for users.
options.note: Pays agent latency and cost for a question answerable in one call.

options.text: Classify the request, then send simple lookups direct and complex work to an agent.
Always run the agent but cap its iterations when the question looks simple.
options.note: Still incurs the orchestration overhead, and the cap is a guess.

options.text: Answer everything with a single call using the largest available model.
options.note: A single call cannot perform a twelve-source comparative study.

en.explanation: These are different workloads. A cheap classifier lets a one-shot lookup stay fast and inexpensive while reserving agent machinery for work that genuinely requires it.
